```{r conversions, include = FALSE}
# basic unit/conversion functions
C_to_f = function(C_val){return(C_val*1.8+32)}
F_to_C = function(F_val){return((F_val-32)/1.8)}
# note these cop conversions are simplified, and assume all heat transferred from CHW to HHW
# in reality some is lost from the chiller, particularly for open drive chillers, and
# this can be relatively large (e.g. 5% of electricity input)
cop_c_to_cop_h = function(cop_c_val){return(cop_c_val+1)}
cop_h_to_cop_c = function(cop_h_val){return(cop_h_val-1)}
cop_h_to_cop_hc = function(cop_h_val){return((cop_h_val*2)-1)}
cop_c_to_cop_hc = function(cop_c_val){return((cop_c_val*2)+1)}
cop_hc_to_cop_c = function(cop_hc){return((cop_hc-1)/2)}
cop_hc_to_cop_h = function(cop_hc){return(((cop_hc-1)/2)+1)}

round_any = function(x, accuracy, f=round){f(x/ accuracy) * accuracy}

# interp1 modified to return
# return 0 for values outside of curve range
interp1_zero <- function(x, y, xi = x, ...) {
    yi <- rep(0, length(xi));
    sel <- which(xi >= range(x)[1] & xi <= range(x)[2]);
    yi[sel] <- interp1(x = x, y = y, xi = xi[sel], ...);
    return(yi);
}

# return 0 for values over max x, return 1 for values under min x
interp1_TES_reset <- function(x, y, xi = x, ...) {
    yi <- rep(0, length(xi));
    over <- xi > range(x)[2];
    under <- xi < range(x)[1];
    yi[!(over|under)] <- interp1(x = x, y = y, xi = xi[!(over|under)], ...);
    yi[under] <- 1;
    return(yi);
}

# peak_hrs = c(16, 17, 18, 19, 20, 21) # CA TOU peak
peak_hr_period = 4 # length(peak_hrs)
```

```{r TES_funcs, include = FALSE}
update_TES_charge = function(hp, load, prev_charge, TES_size){
  available_delta = hp - load

  low_lim = 0
  min( # smaller of calculated and max size
    TES_size,
    max( # larger of 0 and prev + delta
      low_lim,
      prev_charge + available_delta
    )
  )
}

OAT_charge_reset = function(df, loop, sizing, equip_sizes){
  oat_lim = c(equip_sizes$design_oat+2, equip_sizes$design_oat+6)# ; print(oat_lim)
  charge_lim = c(1, 0)
  df = df |>
    mutate(maintain_tes_oat = interp1_TES_reset(oat_lim, charge_lim, oa_t))
  if (str_detect(loop, "chw")) {
    df = df |>
      mutate(maintain_tes_oat = 0)
  }

  
  if (str_detect(sizing, "2x")) {
    load_leveling_size = equip_sizes$TES / 2
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "0.5x")) {
    load_leveling_size = equip_sizes$TES
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "3x")) {
    load_leveling_size = equip_sizes$TES / 3
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "4x")) {
    load_leveling_size = equip_sizes$TES / 4
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "5x")) {
    load_leveling_size = equip_sizes$TES / 5
  } else {
    load_leveling_size = equip_sizes$TES
  }

  df = df |>
    mutate(TES_charge_target_oat = maintain_tes_oat * load_leveling_size) |>
    mutate(design_oat = equip_sizes$design_oat)

  return(df)
}

optimal_charge_reset = function(df, equip_sizes, ctrl_var){
  ctrl_lim = c(0, 1)
  charge_lim = c(1, 0)

  df = df |>
    group_by(date) |>
    mutate(ctrl = as.vector(normalize(.data[[ctrl_var]]))) |>
    ungroup() |> 
    mutate(maintain_tes_optimal = interp1_TES_reset(ctrl_lim, charge_lim, ctrl)) |>
    mutate(TES_charge_target_optimal = maintain_tes_optimal * equip_sizes$TES)

  return(df)
}

optimal_charging_hrs = function(df, loop, control, cap_var){
  hp_operation_hrs = df |> 
    summarize(total_wh = sum(.data[[loop]]), daily_design_cap = min(.data[[cap_var]][.data[[cap_var]] != 0])) 

  if (!(str_detect(control, "predictive"))) {
    # if not predictive, shift total_wh to be prev. day loads
    hp_operation_hrs = hp_operation_hrs |> 
      ungroup() |>
      mutate(total_wh = lag(total_wh, default = 24)) |>
      mutate(daily_design_cap = lag(daily_design_cap, default = 1))
  } # operate HP all day for the first day

  hp_operation_hrs = hp_operation_hrs |> 
    mutate(hrs_hp = ceil(total_wh/daily_design_cap))

  return(hp_operation_hrs)
}

# for storage priority controls
efficiency_var = function(loop){
  if (str_detect(loop, "hhw")) {
    eff = "awhp_cop_h"
  } else if (str_detect(loop, "chw")) {
    eff = "awhp_cop_c"
  }
  return(eff)
}

hp_tes_operation = function(df, loop, control, control_var, cap_var, equip_sizes){
  df = df |> mutate(date = date(datetime)) |> group_by(date)

  if (str_detect(control, "continuous")) {

    if (str_detect(control, "optimal_charging_hours")) { # continuous, optimal charging w/ calc. hours
      hp_operation_hrs = optimal_charging_hrs(df, loop, control, cap_var)

      df = df |>
        left_join(hp_operation_hrs, by = "date") |>
        mutate(total_var = slide_dbl(.data[[control_var]], sum, .before = max(0, hrs_hp[1]-1), .complete = T)) |>
        arrange(date, total_var) |>
        group_by(date) |>
        mutate(operate_hp_tes = ((datetime <= datetime[1] & datetime >= datetime[1]-dhours(max(0, hrs_hp[1]-1)))))
        # operate during best (i.e. lowest) hours block
    
    } else if (str_detect(control, "optimal_charging_reset")) {  # continuous, optimal charging w/ charge reset
      df = df |> mutate(operate_hp_tes = FALSE)

    } else {  # continuous, not optimal charging
      df = df |>
        mutate(total_var = slide_dbl(.data[[control_var]], sum, .before = peak_hr_period-1, .complete = T)) |>
        arrange(date, desc(total_var)) |>
        group_by(date) |>
        mutate(operate_hp_tes = !(datetime <= datetime[1] & datetime >= datetime[1]-dhours(peak_hr_period-1))) #|>
        # do not operate during worst (i.e. highest) hours
        # mutate(test_op_end = datetime[1], test_op_start = datetime[1]-dhours(peak_hr_period-1))

      # debugging
      # if (df$building[1] == "180" & control == "emissions_continuous") {
      #   printer = df |> 
      #     filter(date == ymd("2023-03-29")) |>
      #     select(building, datetime, .data[[control_var]], total_var, operate_hp_tes) |>
      #     arrange(datetime)
      #   print(printer, n=Inf)
      # }
    }

  } else {
    if (str_detect(control, "optimal_charging_hours")) {  # not continuous, optimal charging w/ calc. hours
      hp_operation_hrs = optimal_charging_hrs(df, loop, control)

      df = df |> 
        left_join(hp_operation_hrs, by = "date") |>
        arrange(date, .data[[control_var]]) |>
        group_by(date) |>
        mutate(rank = row_number()) |> 
        mutate(operate_hp_tes = (rank <= hrs_hp))

    } else if (str_detect(control, "optimal_charging_reset")) {  # not continuous, optimal charging w/ charge reset
      df = df |> ungroup() |>
        mutate(operate_hp_tes = FALSE)
      
    } else { # not continuous, not optimal charging
      df = df |>
        arrange(date, desc(.data[[control_var]])) |> 
        # sort by worst emissions hours
        group_by(date) |>
        mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
        mutate(operate_hp_tes = (rank > peak_hr_period))
        # operate for all hours after the peak length 
    }
  }

  df = df |> ungroup() |> arrange(datetime) #arrange(month_pos, day, hour)
  return(df)
}
```

```{r TES_sizing, include = FALSE}
equip_sizing = function(df, loop, sizing, control, hp_curve){ 
  # df is one building's 8760
  # loop is 'hhw' or 'chw'
  df_peak = peak_dates(df, loop)
  peakdate = head(df_peak, 1)$date
  peakdate_hrs = head(df_peak, 1)$num_hrs
  peakdayloads = filter(df, date(datetime) == peakdate)

  # rolling 24-hr peak instead of by date
  # peakdate_hrs = 24
  # peakdate_end = head(df_peak, 1)$hr_id
  # peakdate_start = peakdate_end - 23
  # peakdayloads = filter(df, hr_id >= peakdate_start, hr_id <= peakdate_end)
  # print(df_peak)

  peakdaytotal = sum(peakdayloads[,loop])
  if (str_detect(sizing, "Partial")) {
    peakdayloads = peakdayloads |>
      mutate(operate_hp = TRUE)

  } else { # full storage

    if (str_detect(control, "emissionsXeff")) {
      cop_var = efficiency_var(loop)
      peakdayloads = peakdayloads |>
        mutate(emissions_1W = elec_emissions_rate * 1 / .data[[cop_var]])
      control_var = "emissions_1W"

    } else if (str_detect(control, "emissions")) {
      control_var = "elec_emissions_rate"

    } else if (str_detect(control, "load")) {
      control_var = loop
    }

    if (str_detect(control, "continuous")) {

      peakdayloads = peakdayloads |>
        mutate(total_var = slide_dbl(.data[[control_var]], sum, .before = peak_hr_period-1, .complete = T)) |>
        arrange(desc(total_var)) |>
        # sort by worst emissions/load hours rolling sum
        mutate(operate_hp = !(datetime <= datetime[1] & datetime >= datetime[1] - dhours(peak_hr_period - 1)))
        # operate for all hours after the peak length 

    } else {

      peakdayloads = peakdayloads |>
        arrange(desc(.data[[control_var]])) |>
        # sort by worst emissions/load hours
        mutate(rank = row_number()) |>
        mutate(operate_hp = (rank > peak_hr_period))
        # operate for all hours after the peak length 
    }  
  }

  off_peak_hrs_length = sum(peakdayloads$operate_hp)
  # print(off_peak_hrs_length)
  hp_size = peakdaytotal/off_peak_hrs_length
  if (str_detect(loop, "hhw")) {
    design_oat_func = min
    cap_var = "cap_h"
  } else if (str_detect(loop, "chw")) {
    design_oat_func = max
    cap_var = "cap_c"
  }
  design_oat = peakdayloads |>
    # filter(operate_hp) |>
    summarize(design_oat = design_oat_func(oa_t)) |>
    pull(design_oat)
  hp_num = hp_size / interp1_zero(hp_curve$oa_t, hp_curve[[cap_var]], design_oat)
  # hp_num = ceil(hp_num)
  # this will break if design_oat is below the lowest operating temp in curve, fix if needed

  peakdayloads = peakdayloads |> 
    arrange(datetime) |>
    # mutate(awhp_cap_h = interp1_zero(hp_curve$oa_t, hp_curve$cap_h, oa_t)) |>
    # mutate(hp = operate_hp * hp_num * awhp_cap_h)
    mutate(hp = operate_hp * hp_size)

  peakdayloads = peakdayloads |> 
    mutate(TES_charge_delta = hp - .data[[loop]]) |>
    mutate(charging = TES_charge_delta > 0, discharging = TES_charge_delta < 0)

  TES_sums = peakdayloads |>
    summarise(sum_charge = sum(TES_charge_delta[charging]), 
      sum_discharge = sum(TES_charge_delta[discharging]))
  if (TES_sums$sum_charge + TES_sums$sum_discharge > 1e-3 ) {
    print(TES_sums)
    stop(glue("TES sizing for building {df$building[1]}, control {control} is incorrect"))
  }
  TES_size = TES_sums$sum_charge

  # debugging
  # if (str_detect(control, "full_storage_priority_emissions_continuous_optimal_charging")) {
  #   # print(df_peak)
  #   # print(peak_hrs)
  #   print(control)
  #   # print(hp_curve)
  #   print(glue("peak day total is {peakdaytotal}"))
  #   print(glue("design oat is {design_oat}"))
  #   print(glue("hp size is {hp_size}"))
  #   print(glue("hp num is {hp_num}"))
  #   print(glue("TES size is {TES_size}"))
  #   print(select(peakdayloads, datetime, oa_t, hhw, elec_emissions_rate, operate_hp, hp, TES_charge_delta, mode), n=24)
  # }

  if (str_detect(sizing, "2x")) {
    TES_size = TES_size * 2
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "0.5x")) {
    TES_size = TES_size * 0.5
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "3x")) {
    TES_size = TES_size * 3
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "4x")) {
    TES_size = TES_size * 4
  } else if (str_detect(sizing, "5x")) {
    TES_size = TES_size * 5
  }
  size = list("hp" = hp_size, "hp_num" = hp_num, "design_oat" = design_oat, "TES" = TES_size)
  # print(size)
  return(size)
}
```

```{r loads_to_site, include = FALSE}
# user defined functions specific to this analysis

loads_to_site_energy = function(equip_scenario, df, detail=T){
  # TLDR: converts the measured loads to site energy consumption 
  #       (typ. electricity, also gas) based on elements of provided scenario
  # args :
  #   equip_scenario  : a single row of a tibble with columns describing the
  #   various elements of that scenario (e.g. boiler model, AWHP model, etc.)
  #   df : ~annual hourly timeseries containing datetime, outdoor drybulb (oa_t), 
  #   heating load (hhw) and cooling load (chw) data for the building/system
  #   detail: logical, controls level of output detail
  # 
  # Assumptions:
  # Heating loads: 
  # first served by WWHP in heat recovery mode (if specified in scenario) 
  # within the specified equipment's capacity range, 
  # followed by AWHP in  # heating mode (if specified) within its capacity range,
  # AWHp capacity either directly specified or sized based on highest # of AWHP
  # required to meet remaining HHW load under outdoor temp conditions 
  # when AWHP can still generate hot water
  # followed by a gas boiler (if specified), 
  # with remaining loads served by electric resistance.
  # 
  # Cooling loads:
  # first served by WWHP in heat recovery mode (if specified in scenario),
  # then by an AWHP in cooling mode (if specified) within its capacity range,
  # with any remaining loads served by an fixed COP chiller (unlimited capacity).
  # 
  # returns
  # timeseries dataframe with results and associated equipment scenario ID
  #
  # todos:
  # model wwhp for cooling only (i.e. generic water cooled chiller instead of fixed COP of 5)
  # add capability to model exhaust air heat recovery for specified cfm at 75F
  # add water consumption for tower water?
  # add utility rates for operating cost est?
  # sizing AWHP based on cooling needs?
  # correctly handle NA values for both loads and OAT. currently
  
  s = equip_scenario
  
  df %<>% mutate(hhw_remainder = hhw, 
               chw_remainder = chw, 
               hr_hhw = NA,
               hr_chw=NA,
               simult_h=NA,
               hr_cop_h=NA,
               awhp_num = NA,
               awhp_hhw=NA,
               awhp_cop_h=NA,
               awhp_cap_h=NA,
               elec = 0,
               elec_hr=0,
               elec_awhp_h = 0,
               elec_awhp_c = 0,
               elec_chiller = 0,
               elec_res = 0,
               gas = 0,
               TES_charge = NA,
               testing = NA
               )
  
  # putting here for now bc needed in tes also, update w checks later
  # extract awhp performance characteristics
  # heating
  if (!is.na(s$awhp_h)){
    awhp_h_curve = awhp_curves %>% filter(awhp_id == s$awhp_h) %>% drop_na(oa_t,cap_h,cop_h) %>% select(oa_t, cop_h,cap_h)
    df%<>%mutate(awhp_cop_h = interp1_zero(awhp_h_curve$oa_t, awhp_h_curve$cop_h, oa_t))  
    df%<>%mutate(awhp_cap_h = interp1_zero(awhp_h_curve$oa_t, awhp_h_curve$cap_h, oa_t)) 
    # cooling
    awhp_c_curve = awhp_curves %>% filter(awhp_id == s$awhp_c) %>% drop_na(oa_t,cap_c,cop_c) %>% select(oa_t, cop_c,cap_c)
    df%<>%mutate(awhp_cop_c = interp1_zero(awhp_c_curve$oa_t, awhp_c_curve$cop_c, oa_t)) 
    df%<>%mutate(awhp_cap_c = interp1_zero(awhp_c_curve$oa_t, awhp_c_curve$cap_c, oa_t))
  }

  if (!is.na(s$hr_wwhp)){
    bldg = df$building[1]
    hr_wwhp_bldg = bldgs |> filter(bldg_id == bldg) |> pull(hr_wwhp)

    # extract wwhp performance characteristics
    hr_plr_curve = hr_wwhp_curves %>% 
      filter(hr_wwhp_id == hr_wwhp_bldg) %>%  # s$hr_wwhp
      # note using diff for buildings does mess up the refrigerant inventory calc, fix if needed
      drop_na(cap_h,cop_h) %>% 
      select(cop_h, cap_h) %>% 
      arrange(cap_h)
    hr_plr_curve$cap_h_to_cap_c = (1-(1/hr_plr_curve$cop_h)) #conversion factor from getting cooling capacity from heating_capacity
    hr_plr_curve$cop_c = cop_h_to_cop_c(hr_plr_curve$cop_h)
    hr_plr_curve$cap_c = hr_plr_curve$cap_h * hr_plr_curve$cap_h_to_cap_c #calculate cooling capacity from heating_capacity
    
    least_waste_heat = hr_plr_curve %>% filter(cop_h == max(cop_h))
    max_cap_h = hr_plr_curve %>% filter(cap_h == max(cap_h)) %>% .$cap_h
    min_cap_h = hr_plr_curve %>% filter(cap_h == min(cap_h)) %>% .$cap_h
    df %<>% mutate(hhw_from_cooling = chw / least_waste_heat$cap_h_to_cap_c)
    df %<>% mutate(chw_from_heating = hhw * least_waste_heat$cap_h_to_cap_c)
    df %<>% mutate(hr_min_cap_h = min_cap_h)
    df %<>% mutate(hr_max_cap_h = max_cap_h)
    df %<>% mutate(hr_min_cap_c = min(hr_plr_curve$cap_c))
    df %<>% mutate(hr_max_cap_c = max(hr_plr_curve$cap_c))
  }

  # lead with TES
  if (!is.na(s$tes)){
    if (s$tes == "hhw") {
      cap_var = "awhp_cap_h"
      curve = awhp_h_curve
    } else if (s$tes  == "chw") {
      cap_var = "awhp_cap_c"
      curve = awhp_c_curve
    }
    tot_awhp_cap = str_c(cap_var, "_total")
    loop_remainder = str_c(s$tes, "_remainder")
    equip_sizes = equip_sizing(df, loop_remainder, s$tes_sizing, s$tes_control, curve)
    df %<>% mutate(hp_num_tes = equip_sizes$hp_num)

    # test = pull(df, testing)
    if (!is.na(s$hr_wwhp)){ # heat recovery logic - hhw tank only atm
      if (str_detect(s$tes, "hhw")) {
        hr_loop = "hr_hhw"
        recoverable = "hhw_from_cooling"
        max_cap = "hr_max_cap_h"
        min_cap = "hr_min_cap_h"
      } else if (str_detect(s$tes, "chw")) {
        hr_loop = "hr_chw"
        recoverable = "chw_from_heating"
        max_cap = "hr_max_cap_c"
        min_cap = "hr_min_cap_c"
      }
      hr_calc = df[[hr_loop]]
      hr_calc[1] = 0
      TES_charge_calc = pull(df, TES_charge)
      TES_charge_calc[1] = equip_sizes$TES

      for (t in 2:nrow(df)){
        avail_charge_delta = equip_sizes$TES - TES_charge_calc[t - 1]
        hr_disabled = min(df[[recoverable]][t], avail_charge_delta + df[[s$tes]][t]) < df[[min_cap]][t]

        hr_calc[t] = ifelse(hr_disabled, 0,
          min(
            df[[recoverable]][t], # limited by max heat recoverable
            avail_charge_delta + df[[s$tes]][t], # limited by available storage + load
            df[[max_cap]][t] # limited by max capacity
          )
        )

        charge_delta = min(
          avail_charge_delta,
          max(
            hr_calc[t] - df[[s$tes]][t], 
            -TES_charge_calc[t - 1] # to limit discharge to prev hour charge
          )
        )
        TES_charge_calc[t] = charge_delta + TES_charge_calc[t - 1] 
      }
      df %<>% mutate(TES_charge = TES_charge_calc)
      
      if (str_detect(s$tes, "hhw")) {
        df %<>% mutate(hr_hhw = hr_calc)
      } else if (str_detect(s$tes, "chw")) {
        df %<>% mutate(hr_chw = hr_calc)
      }

    } else { # AWHP-only logic, OAT-based reset to maintain min capacity
      df %<>% mutate(!!tot_awhp_cap := .data[[cap_var]] * equip_sizes$hp_num)
      # print(s$desc)
      # print(equip_sizes)

      if (str_detect(s$tes_control, "hp_priority")) {
        df %<>% mutate(operate_hp_tes = TRUE, hp_tes = .data[[tot_awhp_cap]])

      } else { # storage priority

        if (str_detect(s$tes_control, "emissionsXeff")) {
          cop_var = efficiency_var(s$tes)
          df = df |>
            mutate(emissions_1W = elec_emissions_rate * 1 / .data[[cop_var]])
          control_var = "emissions_1W"

        } else if (str_detect(s$tes_control, "emissions")) {
          control_var = "elec_emissions_rate"

        } else if (str_detect(s$tes_control, "load")) {
          control_var = s$tes
        }

        if (!(str_detect(s$tes_control, "predictive"))) {
          lagged_control_var = str_c(control_var, "_lagged")
          lagged_df = df |>
            mutate(datetime = datetime + hours(24)) |>
            select(building, datetime, .data[[control_var]]) |>
            rename(!!lagged_control_var := !!control_var)
          df = df |> ungroup() |>
            left_join(lagged_df, by = c("building", "datetime"))
        } else {
          lagged_control_var = control_var
        }

        df = df |> 
          hp_tes_operation(loop_remainder, s$tes_control, lagged_control_var, tot_awhp_cap, equip_sizes)
          
        if (!(str_detect(s$tes_control, "predictive"))) {
          # operate fully for the first day
          df = df |> mutate(operate_hp_tes = ifelse(date(datetime) == date(datetime[1]), TRUE, operate_hp_tes))
        }

        df = df |> mutate(hp_tes = operate_hp_tes * .data[[tot_awhp_cap]])
      }

      df = OAT_charge_reset(df, s$tes, s$tes_sizing, equip_sizes)
      if (str_detect(s$tes_control, "optimal_charging_reset")) {
        df = df |>
          optimal_charge_reset(equip_sizes, control_var) |> # check if using
          mutate(TES_charge_target = pmax(TES_charge_target_optimal, TES_charge_target_oat))
      } else {
        df = df |> rename(TES_charge_target = TES_charge_target_oat)
      }
      hp_tes_reset = pull(df, hp_tes)
      hp_tes_reset[1] = df[[tot_awhp_cap]][1]
      TES_charge_reset = pull(df, TES_charge)
      TES_charge_reset[1] = equip_sizes$TES

      for (t in 2:nrow(df)){
        TES_prev = TES_charge_reset[t - 1]
        deficit = max(0, df$TES_charge_target[t] - TES_prev)

        if (deficit > 0) {
          hp_tes_reset[t] = min(df[[tot_awhp_cap]][t], deficit + df[[loop_remainder]][t])
        }
        
        TES_charge_reset[t] = update_TES_charge(
          hp_tes_reset[t],
          df[[loop_remainder]][t],
          TES_prev,
          equip_sizes$TES
        )

        # below is for situations where deficit is 0 (previous hour charge meets target), and control logic might disable HP operation (based on emissions etc)
        # but this lowers the charge below target (tank is serving loads when it should not be), so check for that and correct
        # if this isn't corrected the charge oscillates as the logic above only checks the previous hour charge
        if (deficit == 0) {
          if (TES_charge_reset[t] < df$TES_charge_target[t]) {
            hp_tes_reset[t] = min(df[[tot_awhp_cap]][t], df[[loop_remainder]][t])
            # test[t] = hp_tes_reset[t]

            TES_charge_reset[t] = update_TES_charge(
              hp_tes_reset[t],
              df[[loop_remainder]][t],
              TES_prev,
              equip_sizes$TES
            )
          }
        }
      }
      df %<>% mutate(hp_tes = hp_tes_reset, TES_charge = TES_charge_reset)
    }

    # debugging
    # if (!(str_detect(s$tes_control, "hp_priority"))) {
    #   print(df |> filter(is.na(TES_avail_charge_delta)) |> select(building, datetime, hhw, operate_hp_tes, hp_tes, TES_avail_charge_delta), n = Inf)
    #   print(df |>
    #     filter(date(datetime) %in% c(ymd("2023-03-11"), ymd("2023-03-12"))) |>
    #     select(building, datetime, hhw, elec_emissions_rate, total_var, test_op_end, test_op_start, operate_hp_tes, hp_tes, TES_avail_charge_delta),
    #     n = Inf)
    # }

    df %<>%
      mutate(TES_charge_delta = TES_charge - lag(TES_charge, default = TES_charge[1])) %<>%
      mutate(!!loop_remainder := .data[[loop_remainder]] + TES_charge_delta) %<>%
      mutate(!!loop_remainder := ifelse(.data[[loop_remainder]] < 1e-3, 0, .data[[loop_remainder]])) %<>%
      mutate(TES_load = ifelse(TES_charge_delta < 0, -TES_charge_delta, 0)) #actual served load
  } else {
    df %<>%
      mutate(TES_charge = 0, TES_charge_delta = 0, TES_load = 0)
  }

  # lead with heat recovery if available
  if (!is.na(s$hr_wwhp)){
    # determine how much simultaneous load there is (accounting for waste heat for wwhp, 
    # leaving some CHW on the table in worst case scenario)
    # todo: more elegant way to resolve this simplification?  
    # to get around requiring cop to determine how much simultaneous load there 
    # is and associated circular reference. not worth the iteration time to 
    # solve given small associated error
    if (is.na(s$tes)){ 
      df%<>%mutate(simult_h = pmin(hhw,chw/least_waste_heat$cap_h_to_cap_c))
      df%<>%mutate(hr_hhw = ifelse(pmin(max_cap_h,simult_h)>=min_cap_h,pmin(max_cap_h,simult_h),0))
      df%<>%mutate(hr_cop_h = ifelse(hr_hhw>0,interp1_zero(hr_plr_curve$cap_h, hr_plr_curve$cop_h, hr_hhw),0))
      df%<>%mutate(hr_chw = ifelse(hr_cop_h==0, 0.0, hr_hhw*(1-(1/hr_cop_h))))
      df%<>%mutate(hr_served_hhw=hr_hhw)
      df%<>%mutate(hr_served_chw=hr_chw)
    } else { # if TES does exist, one of hr_hhw/hr_chw has already been calculated
      if (str_detect(s$tes, "hhw")) { # this will NOT work with switchover logic since some of these columns would be partly calc differently
        df%<>%mutate(hr_cop_h = ifelse(hr_hhw>0,interp1_zero(hr_plr_curve$cap_h, hr_plr_curve$cop_h, hr_hhw),0))
        df%<>%mutate(hr_chw = ifelse(hr_cop_h==0, 0.0, hr_hhw*(1-(1/hr_cop_h))))
        df%<>%mutate(hr_served_hhw=hr_hhw-pmax(0,TES_charge_delta))
        df%<>%mutate(hr_served_chw=hr_chw)
      } else if (str_detect(s$tes, "chw")) {
        df%<>%mutate(hr_cop_c = ifelse(hr_chw>0,interp1_zero(hr_plr_curve$cap_c, hr_plr_curve$cop_c, hr_chw),0))
        df%<>%mutate(hr_hhw = ifelse(hr_cop_c==0, 0.0, hr_chw*(1+(1/hr_cop_c))))
        df%<>%mutate(hr_cop_h = ifelse(hr_hhw>0,interp1_zero(hr_plr_curve$cap_h, hr_plr_curve$cop_h, hr_hhw),0))
        df%<>%mutate(hr_served_chw=hr_chw-pmax(0,TES_charge_delta))
        df%<>%mutate(hr_served_hhw=hr_hhw)
      }
    }
    df%<>%mutate(hhw_remainder = hhw_remainder-hr_hhw)
    df%<>%mutate(chw_remainder = chw_remainder-hr_chw)
    df%<>%mutate(elec_hr=ifelse(hr_cop_h>0,hr_hhw/hr_cop_h,0))
    df%<>%mutate(elec=elec+elec_hr)
  } 
  
  # then awhp if available
  if (!is.na(s$awhp_h)){
    # extract awhp performance characteristics
    # awhp_h_curve = awhp_curves %>% filter(awhp_id == s$awhp_h) %>% drop_na(oa_t,cap_h,cop_h) %>% select(oa_t, cop_h,cap_h)
    # df%<>%mutate(awhp_cop_h = interp1_zero(awhp_h_curve$oa_t, awhp_h_curve$cop_h, oa_t))  
    # df%<>%mutate(awhp_cap_h = interp1_zero(awhp_h_curve$oa_t, awhp_h_curve$cap_h, oa_t))  

    # determine actual number of AWHPs based on equipment sizing scenario
    if (str_detect(s$awhp_sizing, "%")) {
      # size number of heat pumps to meet 
      # find max HHW load at OATs where
      # which that AWHP can generate HHW
      max_num_awhps_h = max(df %>% drop_na(hhw_remainder,awhp_cap_h) %>% 
                            filter(awhp_cap_h>0)%>% mutate(num_awhps = hhw_remainder/awhp_cap_h) %>% .$num_awhps)
      max_num_awhps_c = max(df %>% drop_na(chw_remainder,awhp_cap_c) %>% 
                            filter(awhp_cap_c>0)%>% mutate(num_awhps = chw_remainder/awhp_cap_c) %>% .$num_awhps)
      max_num_awhps = max_num_awhps_h
      # max_num_awhps = max(max_num_awhps_h, max_num_awhps_c)
      # if (!is.na(s$tes)){
      #   if (str_detect(s$tes, "hhw")) {
      #     max_num_awhps = max_num_awhps_h
      #   } else if (str_detect(s$tes, "chw")) {
      #     max_num_awhps = max_num_awhps_c
      #   }
      # } else {
      #   max_num_awhps = max_num_awhps_h
      # }
      
      target_frac = as.numeric(str_extract(s$awhp_sizing, "[:digit:]*(?=%)"))/100
      
      if (str_detect(s$awhp_sizing, "RoundUp")) {
        # assign number of AWHPs based on min # of heat pumps required to serve 
        # that load fully 
        df%<>%mutate(awhp_num = ceiling(target_frac*max_num_awhps))
      } else{
        # use fractional heat pumps based on percentage
        df%<>%mutate(awhp_num = target_frac* max_num_awhps)
      }
    } else{
      # assumes that user specified number (or fraction) of heat pumps
      df%<>%mutate(awhp_num = as.numeric(s$awhp_sizing))
    }
    df%<>%mutate(awhp_hhw = ifelse(awhp_cap_h*awhp_num > hhw_remainder, hhw_remainder, awhp_cap_h*awhp_num))
    # df%<>%mutate(awhp_hhw_overmax = pmax(awhp_hhw-awhp_cap_h_total, 0)) 
    if (is.na(s$tes)){
      df%<>%mutate(awhp_cap_h_total = awhp_num*awhp_cap_h)
    }
    df%<>%mutate(hhw_remainder = hhw_remainder-awhp_hhw) 
    df%<>%mutate(backup_hhw = hhw_remainder) 
    df%<>%mutate(elec_awhp_h = ifelse(awhp_hhw>0 | awhp_cop_h>0,awhp_hhw/awhp_cop_h,0))  
    df%<>%mutate(elec = elec+elec_awhp_h)
  }
  # then gas boiler if available
  # assume boiler capacity is unlimited
  if (!is.na(s$boiler)){
    boiler = boilers %>% filter(boiler_id == s$boiler)
    df%<>%
      mutate(gas=hhw_remainder/boiler$eff) %>% # updated to divide
      mutate(hhw_remainder = ifelse(is.na(hhw_remainder),NA,0))
  } 
  # remaining HHW load assumed served by electric resistance 
  # (e.g. elec boiler, or awhp resistance backup)
  if (sum(df$hhw_remainder,na.rm=T)>0){
    df%<>%
      mutate(elec_res = hhw_remainder) %>% 
      mutate(elec=elec+elec_res) %>% 
      mutate(hhw_remainder = ifelse(is.na(hhw_remainder),NA,0))
  } else {
    df%<>%
      mutate(elec_res = 0)
  }
  
  # if awhp is specified in cooling, it is assumed to be used here
  # e.g. use to easily model an air_cooled chiller, or use of AWHP for cooling
  if (!is.na(s$awhp_c)){
    # awhp_c_curve = awhp_curves %>% filter(awhp_id == s$awhp_c) %>% drop_na(oa_t,cap_c,cop_c) %>% select(oa_t, cop_c,cap_c)
    # df%<>%mutate(awhp_cop_c = interp1_zero(awhp_c_curve$oa_t, awhp_c_curve$cop_c, oa_t)) 
    # df%<>%mutate(awhp_cap_c = interp1_zero(awhp_c_curve$oa_t, awhp_c_curve$cap_c, oa_t))
    
    df%<>%mutate(awhp_chw = ifelse(awhp_cap_c*awhp_num > chw_remainder, chw_remainder,awhp_cap_c*awhp_num))
    df%<>%mutate(chw_remainder = chw_remainder-awhp_chw)
    
    df%<>%mutate(elec_awhp_c = ifelse(awhp_chw >0 & awhp_cop_c>0,awhp_chw/awhp_cop_c,0))
    df%<>%mutate(elec = elec+elec_awhp_c)
  }
  
  # remaining CHW load assumed to be served by water cooled chiller (todo: fixed COP 5)
  # 09.02 changing to air cooled
  if (sum(df$chw_remainder,na.rm=T)>0){
    chiller_COP = 2.84
    df%<>%
      mutate(chiller_chw = chw_remainder) %>% 
      mutate(elec_chiller = chw_remainder/chiller_COP) %>% 
      mutate(elec=elec+elec_chiller) %>% 
      mutate(chw_remainder = ifelse(is.na(chw_remainder),NA,0))
  }
  
  if(!detail){
    # return just the loads and outdoor temps to reduce resources
    df %<>% select(datetime, oa_t, elec, gas)
  }
  # calculate total refrigerant inventory based on number of AWHPs and HRCs
  df %<>% 
    mutate(total_refrig_emissions_inventory = 0) %>% 
    mutate(total_refrig_emissions_inventory = 
             ifelse(is.na(s$awhp_refrig_emissions_inventory),0,s$awhp_refrig_emissions_inventory*awhp_num) + 
             ifelse(is.na(s$hr_wwhp_refrig_emissions_inventory),0,s$hr_wwhp_refrig_emissions_inventory))

  # store eq_scen_id in df before returning from function (for later joining)
  df %<>%  mutate(eq_scen_id = s$eq_scen_id)
  
  # have to set data (regardless of equipment scenario) 
  # to NA if OAT is missing it would skew any AWHP vs non AWHP scenarios
  df %<>%
    mutate(elec = ifelse(is.na(hhw) | is.na(oa_t), NA, elec)) %<>%
    mutate(gas = ifelse(is.na(hhw) | is.na(oa_t), NA, gas))         
  
  return(df)
}
```

```{r grid_emissions, include = FALSE}
# compute grid emissions rate 
grid_emissions = function(emissions_scenario, df){
  s = emissions_scenario
  df%<>%mutate(em_scen_id = s$em_scen_id)
  
  # handle misc input possibilities for grid region
  if ('grid_region' %in% names(s)){
    # grid region defined in scenario
    # if (is.na(s$grid_region)){
    #   # but is NA
    #   # if the user provides a grid region in the emissions scenarios
    #   # assume it is provided in the timeseries df
    #   s$grid_region = "CAISO"
    #   df%<>% mutate(grid_region = s$grid_region)    
    # } else{
      # use the specified grid region in the emissions scenario
      # and add to the results df
      df%<>% mutate(grid_region = s$grid_region)
    # }    
  } else {
    if ('grid_region' %in% names(df)) {
      # nothing defined in emissions scenario, but dataset includes grid region
      s$grid_region = df%>%distinct(grid_region) %>% .$grid_region
    } else {
      # nothing defined in emissions scenarios or in dataset
      s$grid_region = "CAISO"
      df%<>% mutate(grid_region = s$grid_region)      
    }
  }

  if (s$emissions_type=="Combustion only"){
    grid_data = grid_scenarios %>% 
      rename(grid_region = gea, grid_scenario = scenario, grid_year = year) %>% 
      inner_join(s) %>%
      mutate(elec_emissions_rate = lrmer_co2e_c*(1-shortrun_weighting)+ srmer_co2e_c*shortrun_weighting) %>% 
      select(month,hour,elec_emissions_rate)

  } else if (s$emissions_type=="Includes pre-combustion") {
    grid_data = grid_scenarios %>% 
      rename(grid_region = gea, grid_scenario = scenario, grid_year = year) %>% 
      inner_join(s) %>%
      mutate(elec_emissions_rate = (lrmer_co2e_c+lrmer_co2e_p)*(1-shortrun_weighting)+ (srmer_co2e_c+srmer_co2e_p)*shortrun_weighting) %>% 
      select(month,hour,elec_emissions_rate)
    
  } else {
    return(F)
  }

  df %<>% 
    # mutate(month=month(datetime), hour=hour(datetime)) %>% 
    inner_join(grid_data)
    # select(-month,-hour)

  # print(select(df, datetime, hhw, month, hour, lrmer_co2e_p, lrmer_co2e_c, srmer_co2e_p, srmer_co2e_c, elec_emissions_rate)) # checking

  return(df)
}
```

```{r site_to_source, include = FALSE}
# converts site energy consumption to source using provided emissions rates
# also estimates fugitive refrigerant related emissions 
site_to_source <- function(emissions_scenario, df){
  s = emissions_scenario

  df%<>%mutate(gas_emissions = s$gas_emissions_rate*gas/1000/1000) #Wh to kWh & g to kg
  
  df%<>%mutate(elec_emissions = elec_emissions_rate*elec/1000/1000) #Wh to kWh & g to kg
  df%<>%mutate(awhp_h_emissions = elec_emissions_rate*elec_awhp_h/1000/1000) #Wh to kWh & g to kg
  df%<>%mutate(elec_h_emissions = elec_emissions_rate*(elec_awhp_h+elec_hr+elec_res)/1000/1000) #Wh to kWh & g to kg
  df%<>%mutate(elec_c_emissions = elec_emissions_rate*(elec_awhp_c+elec_hr+elec_chiller)/1000/1000) #Wh to kWh & g to kg
  
  df%<>%
    mutate(refrig_emissions = total_refrig_emissions_inventory*s$annual_refrig_leakage/8760)

  return(df)
}
```

```{r scenario_analysis, include = FALSE}
# higher level function
# for assessing different equipment and emissions scenarios (combined, full factorial)
scenario_analysis <- function(df, equip_scenarios, emissions_scenarios, detail=T){
  # add'l first step for emissions-based TES control
  emissions_data = emissions_scenarios %>% 
    split(.$em_scen_id) %>% 
    map(grid_emissions, df=df) %>% 
    list_rbind() 
  # print(emissions_data) 

  equip_loads = equip_scenarios %>% 
    split(.$eq_scen_id) %>% 
    map(loads_to_site_energy, df=emissions_data, detail=detail) %>% 
    list_rbind()
    
  results = emissions_scenarios %>% 
    split(.$em_scen_id) %>% 
    map(site_to_source, df=equip_loads) %>% 
    list_rbind()    
  
  return(results)
}
```

```{r dataprep, include = FALSE}
# Read in data, misc initial prep/cleaning tasks

# tables of relevant information
bldgs <- "./data/bldg.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3)  |> mutate(bldg_id = as.character(bldg_id))
refrigs <- "./data/refrigs.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3)
awhps <- "./data/awhps.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3)
hr_wwhps <- "./data/hr_wwhps.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3)
boilers <- "./data/boilers.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3)
awhp_curves <- "./data/awhp_curves.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3)
hr_wwhp_curves <- "./data/hr_wwhp_curves.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3)
plot_dates <- "./data/loads/plot_dates.csv" %>% read_csv(skip=3) |> mutate(date = dmy(date))

awhp_curves%<>%
  mutate(oa_t = ifelse(unit_system == "IP",F_to_C(oa_t),oa_t),
         cap_c = ifelse(unit_system == "IP",ton_to_W*cap_c,cap_c),
         cap_h = ifelse(unit_system == "IP",BTUh_to_W*cap_h,cap_h)) %>% 
  select(-unit_system)

# assume/simplify that AWHPs can continue making HHW even at high OATs,
# even if the performance curve data does not show that they can
max_oat_awhp_h = awhp_curves %>% group_by(awhp_id) %>% filter(cap_h >0) %>% filter(oa_t == max(oa_t)) %>% mutate(oa_t =60)
awhp_curves %<>% add_row(max_oat_awhp_h)

hr_wwhp_curves%<>%
  mutate(cap_h = ifelse(unit_system == "IP",BTUh_to_W*cap_h,cap_h))

# load in elec emissions rates
grid_scenarios = readRDS("./data/grid_scenarios.rds")
# if needed, extract updated information from the latest cambium data

df = df |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(hhw = ifelse(hhw < 0, NA, hhw), chw = ifelse(chw < 0, NA, chw)) |> # set negative load hours to account for common measurement error issues/simplification 
  mutate(datetime = with_tz(datetime, "US/Pacific")) |> # set local datetime
  mutate(month = month(datetime), day = day(datetime), hour = hour(datetime)) |>
  # mutate(month_pos = case_when( # to start the year in june
  #       month >= 6 ~ month - 6,
  #       month <= 5 ~ month + 7)) |>
  filter(!is.na(hhw), !is.na(chw), !is.na(oa_t)) |>
  mutate(hr_id = row_number()) |>
  inner_join(bldgs, by = join_by(building == bldg_id)) |>
  arrange(building, datetime) #month_pos, day, hour)
```

``` {r scenarios_define, include = FALSE}
)
```

``` {r scenarios_prep, include = FALSE}
equip_scenarios%<>%
  rowid_to_column("eq_scen_id") 

# extract refrigerant emission inventory (total kgCO2e) for these 
# equipment scenarios
equip_scenarios %<>%  
    left_join(awhps %>% select(awhp_id,refrig_id,charge) %>% rename(awhp_h = awhp_id)) %>%
    left_join(refrigs %>% select(refrig_id,gwp)) %>% 
    mutate(awhp_refrig_emissions_inventory = gwp*charge) %>% 
    select(-charge, -refrig_id, -gwp) %>% 
    left_join(hr_wwhps %>% select(hr_wwhp_id,refrig_id,charge) %>% rename(hr_wwhp = hr_wwhp_id)) %>%
    left_join(refrigs %>% select(refrig_id,gwp)) %>% 
    mutate(hr_wwhp_refrig_emissions_inventory = gwp*charge) %>% 
    select(-charge, -refrig_id, -gwp) %>%
    mutate(legend = str_c(eq_scen_id, " - ", desc))
    

# combinatorial expansion of different grid scenarios
emissions_scenarios = 
  expand_grid(
    annual_refrig_leakage = 0.05,
    # grid_region = "CAISO", # if grid region is specified here (e.g. "CAISO") it will override whatever is entered in the bldg table (allows testing out moving buildings to other grid regions, of dubious value) 
    grid_scenario = c("MidCase"), #c("MidCase", "Decarb95by2050", "HighDemandGrowth"),
    grid_year = c(2025), #c(2025,2030,2035,2040,2045, 2050),
    emissions_type = c("Includes pre-combustion"), #c("Combustion only","Includes pre-combustion") 
    shortrun_weighting = 0, # seq(0,1), #weighting between short and long run emissions
    gas_emissions_rate = ng_combustion_to_co2e,
  ) 

emissions_scenarios%<>%
  rowid_to_column("em_scen_id")
```

```{r run_model_multi, include = FALSE}
results_all = df %>% 
  mutate(splitter = building) %>% 
  group_by(splitter) %>%
  group_map( ~ scenario_analysis(df=., equip_scenarios=equip_scenarios, 
                      emissions_scenarios=emissions_scenarios, 
                      detail=T)) %>% 
  list_rbind() %>% 
  left_join(select(equip_scenarios, eq_scen_id, tes_sizing, tes_control_id, desc),
    by = "eq_scen_id")

# results_all |>
#   group_by(building, desc) |>
#   filter(!(desc %in% c("BaselineGas", "No TES"))) |>
#   filter(TES_charge[n()] < TES_charge[1]) |>
#   distinct(building, desc)

# correct for end-of-year charge
for (id in bldgs$bldg_id) {
    for (d in equip_scenarios$desc) {
      if (!(d %in% c("BaselineGas", "No TES"))) {
        bldg_results = filter(results_all, building == id, desc == d)
        final_timestamp = tail(bldg_results, n = 1)
        initial_timestamp = head(bldg_results, n = 1)
        if (final_timestamp$TES_charge < initial_timestamp$TES_charge) {
          delta = initial_timestamp$TES_charge - final_timestamp$TES_charge
          # percent = 100*delta/initial_timestamp$TES_charge
          nom_cap = head(bldg_results, 1)$awhp_cap_h_total
          hrs = 3 + delta / nom_cap  # 3 hrs extra for safety since not sure what the next hours look like
          # print(hrs)
          awhp_operate = delta / hrs
          extra_df = head(bldg_results, hrs) |> 
            mutate(
              datetime = datetime+years(1),
              awhp_hhw = awhp_operate,
              elec_awhp_h = awhp_hhw/awhp_cop_h,
              elec = elec_awhp_h,
              awhp_h_emissions = elec_emissions_rate*elec_awhp_h/1000/1000,
              elec_h_emissions = awhp_h_emissions,
              elec_emissions = awhp_h_emissions
            )
          results_all = rbind(results_all, extra_df)
        }
      }
  }
}
```

```{r hr_actual, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
plt_hr_actual = results_all |>
  # filter(desc == "No TES") |>
  # mutate(hhw_check = awhp_hhw + hr_hhw - hhw) |> filter(hhw_check > 1e-2)
  group_by(building, eq_scen_id) |>
  summarize(total_hhw = sum(hhw), total_awhp_hhw = sum(awhp_hhw), total_hr_hhw = sum(hr_served_hhw), total_tes_chw = sum(TES_load), total_chw = sum(chw), total_awhp_chw = sum(awhp_chw), total_chiller_chw = sum(chiller_chw), total_hr_chw = sum(hr_served_chw)) |>
  mutate(awhp_hhw_served = total_awhp_hhw/total_hhw, hr_hhw_served = total_hr_hhw/total_hhw, tes_chw_served = total_tes_chw/total_chw, awhp_chw_served = total_awhp_chw/total_chw, hr_chw_served = total_hr_chw/total_chw, chiller_chw_served = total_chiller_chw/total_chw) |>
  # print(n=Inf)
  pivot_longer(cols = c(awhp_hhw_served, hr_hhw_served, tes_chw_served, awhp_chw_served, hr_chw_served, chiller_chw_served), names_to = "equipment",  values_to = "load_served") |>
  mutate(load_type = ifelse(equipment %in% c("awhp_hhw_served", "hr_hhw_served", "tes_hhw_served"), "HHW", "CHW")) |>
  mutate(equip_group = case_when(
      equipment %in% c("awhp_hhw_served", "awhp_chw_served") ~ "AWHP",
      equipment %in% c("hr_hhw_served", "hr_chw_served") ~ "HR WWHP",
      equipment %in% c("tes_hhw_served", "tes_chw_served") ~ "TES",
      equipment == "chiller_chw_served" ~ "Chiller")) |>
  ggplot() +
    geom_col(aes(eq_scen_id, load_served, fill=equip_group)) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = equip_scenarios$eq_scen_id) +
    # scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1.001), breaks = seq(0, 1, 0.1), labels = percent(seq(0,1,0.1))) +
    labs(x = "", y = "Percentage of HHW Load", title = "Distribution of load served by equipment", fill = "Equipment", shape = "") +
    geom_point(data = equip_scenarios, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, shape = legend), alpha=0) +
    scale_fill_manual(values=cal_palette4[4:1]) +
    facet_grid(load_type ~ building)
```

```{r hr_potential, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
plt_hr_potential = results_all |>
  # filter(desc == "No TES") |>
  mutate(date = date(datetime)) |>
  mutate(hhw_not_recovered = pmax(0, hhw_from_cooling - hr_hhw),
    hhw_after_hr = pmax(0, hhw - hr_hhw),
    hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim = ifelse(
      hhw_from_cooling < hr_min_cap_h, 0, # limited by recoverable load from chw, if that's below the minimum then nothing can be done
      pmin(hhw_not_recovered, hr_max_cap_h - hr_hhw) # smaller of what was not recovered and max. cap minus what was actually recovered
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(chw_not_recovered = pmax(0, chw_from_heating - hr_chw),
    chw_after_hr = pmax(0, chw - hr_chw),
    chw_not_recovered_cap_lim = ifelse(
      chw_from_heating < hr_min_cap_c, 0, # limited by recoverable load from hhw, if that's below the minimum then nothing can be done
      pmin(chw_not_recovered, hr_max_cap_c - hr_chw) # smaller of what was not recovered and max. cap minus what was actually recovered
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(building, eq_scen_id, desc, date) |>
  # select(datetime, hhw, chw, hhw_from_cooling, hr_hhw, hhw_not_recovered)
  summarize(total_hhw = sum(hhw), total_chw = sum(chw),
    total_hhw_after_hr = sum(hhw_after_hr),
    total_chw_after_hr = sum(chw_after_hr),
    total_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim = sum(hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim),
    total_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim = sum(chw_not_recovered_cap_lim)) |>
  mutate(
    total_useful_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim = pmin(total_hhw_after_hr, total_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim),
    total_useful_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim = pmin(total_chw_after_hr, total_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim),
  ) |>
  mutate(month = month(date, label = T)) |>
  mutate(quarter = quarter(date)) |>
  mutate(season = case_when(
    quarter == 1 ~ "Jan-Mar",
    quarter == 2 ~ "Apr-Jun",
    quarter == 3 ~ "Jul-Sep",
    quarter == 4 ~ "Oct-Dec",
  )) |>
  # filter(building == "181", eq_scen_id==2)
  ungroup() |> group_by(building, eq_scen_id, desc, quarter, season) |>
  summarize(total_hhw = sum(total_hhw),
    total_chw = sum(total_chw),
    total_useful_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim = sum(total_useful_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim),
    total_useful_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim = sum(total_useful_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    total_useful_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim_percent = total_useful_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim/total_hhw,
    total_useful_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim_percent = total_useful_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim/total_chw
  ) |>
  # filter(building == "181")
  pivot_longer(cols = c(total_useful_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim_percent, total_useful_chw_not_recovered_cap_lim_percent), names_to = "ratio_name", values_to="ratio") |>
  mutate(load_type = ifelse(ratio_name == "total_useful_hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim_percent", "From CHW, to serve HHW", "From HHW, to serve CHW")) |>
  # filter(building == "180", eq_scen_id==2)
  ggplot() +
    geom_col(aes(reorder(season, quarter), ratio), fill = "orange") +
    # geom_point(data = equip_scenarios, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, shape = legend), alpha=0) +
    labs(x = "", y = "", title = "Ratio of useful load not recovered to total load", shape = "") +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,1)) +
    theme(legend.position = "top") +
    facet_nested(building ~ load_type + reorder(desc, eq_scen_id))
```

```{r hr potential timeseries, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
dat = results_all |>
  mutate(month = month(datetime, label = T), year = year(datetime)) |>
  filter(building == "205", desc == "No TES", month == "Dec", year == 2021) |> # 
  mutate(hhw_not_recovered = hhw_from_cooling - hr_hhw,
    hhw_after_hr = hhw - hr_hhw,
    hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim = ifelse(hhw_not_recovered > hr_max_cap_h, hr_max_cap_h, hhw_not_recovered)
  )

below_min = dat |>
  select(datetime, hhw, hhw_from_cooling, hr_min_cap_h) |>
  mutate(below = (hhw_from_cooling < hr_min_cap_h), group = cumsum(below != lag(below, default = FALSE))) |>
  filter(below == TRUE) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarize(xmin = min(datetime), xmax = max(datetime)+hours(1))

dat |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(hhw, hhw_from_cooling, hr_hhw, hhw_not_recovered_cap_lim), names_to = 'meter', values_to = 'value') |>
  ggplot() +
    geom_line(aes(datetime, value, color=meter), alpha=0.8) +
    geom_line(aes(datetime, hr_min_cap_h), color="red", linetype=2) +
    geom_rect(data = below_min, aes(xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax, ymin=0, ymax=Inf), fill = "yellow", alpha=0.1)
```

```{r totals, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
# filtered_results |> # elec, elec_hr, elec_res, elec_awhp_c, elec_chiller, 
emissions_var = "awhp_h_emissions" #elec_emissions
baseline = summary |> 
  filter(desc == "No TES") |>
  rename(elec_emissions_base = elec_emissions) |>
  rename(elec_h_emissions_base = elec_h_emissions) |>
  select(building, elec_emissions_base, elec_h_emissions_base)

plt_tot = summary |>
  left_join(baseline, by = "building") |>
  filter(desc != "No TES") |>
  mutate(elec_emissions_diff = 100*(elec_emissions - elec_emissions_base)/elec_emissions_base) |>
  mutate(elec_h_emissions_diff = 100*(elec_h_emissions - elec_h_emissions_base)/elec_h_emissions_base) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = c(elec_emissions_diff, elec_h_emissions_diff), names_to = "emissions_diff", values_to = "value") |>
  ggplot(aes(tes_control_id, value, fill = emissions_diff)) + 
    geom_col(aes(fill = emissions_diff), color = 'black', position = position_dodge(width = 0.9)) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = percent(value/100, accuracy = 1, style_positive = "plus")),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
      vjust=1.8) +
    geom_point(data = tes_control_scenarios, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, shape = tes_legend), alpha=0, inherit.aes=FALSE) +
    labs(y="Percentage difference", x = "Control strategy", title = "Electricity use emissions compared to no-TES scenario", shape="", fill="") +
    theme(legend.position="top") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = tes_control_scenarios$tes_control_id) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits=c(-60,10), breaks = seq(-60, 10, 10), labels = percent(seq(-0.6,0.1,0.1))) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("elec_emissions_diff" = "orange", "elec_h_emissions_diff" = "red"), labels = c("elec_emissions_diff" = "Total", "elec_h_emissions_diff" = "Heating")) +
    facet_grid(reorder(tes_sizing, eq_scen_id) ~ building)
```

```{r equip_sizes, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
baseline_sizes = summary |> 
  filter(desc == "No TES") |>
  rename(awhp_base = AWHP_num) |>
  select(building, awhp_base)

equip_scenarios_plot = tes_control_scenarios |>
  # filter(desc!="No TES") |>
  select(tes_legend) |>
  add_row(tes_legend = "<span style='color:red'># = unmet hours</span>")

sizes = summary |>
  left_join(baseline_sizes, by = "building") |>
  # mutate(AWHP = (awhp_hhw - awhp_base)/awhp_base,
  mutate(AWHP = 100*(AWHP_num - awhp_base)/awhp_base,
  AWHP_actual = 100*(AWHP_num_over - awhp_base)/awhp_base,
  AWHP_actual = ifelse(abs(AWHP - AWHP_actual) < 1, NA, AWHP_actual)
  # tes_diff = 100*(TES - tes_base)/tes_base # this is zero since baseline is no TES
  )
  # select(building, desc, AWHP_size, AWHP_size_over, awhp_base, AWHP, AWHP_actual)
  # pivot_longer(cols = c(awhp_hhw, TES_charge), names_to = 'equipment', values_to = 'size') |>
plt_sizes = sizes |>
  filter(desc != "No TES") |>
    # select(building, desc, equipment, size)
  ggplot() + 
    geom_col(aes(tes_control_id, AWHP, fill = "AWHP"), color = 'orange') +
    geom_col(aes(tes_control_id, AWHP_actual, fill = "AWHP_actual"), color = 'orange', alpha=0.7) +
    geom_text(aes(tes_control_id, AWHP, label = percent(AWHP/100, accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")), vjust=1.5) +
```

``` {r TES_utilization_hours, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
plt_util_hrs = results_all |>
```

```{r aggregated timeseries, hour, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
TES_var = "TES_charge"
plt_hr = function(df, scen, equip_scenarios) {
  scen_desc = equip_scenarios$desc[scen]
  plt = df |>
    filter(eq_scen_id == scen) |>
    mutate(month = month(datetime, label=T), hour = hour(datetime)) |>
    select(building, month, hour, awhp_hhw, .data[[TES_var]]) |>
    group_by(building, month, hour) |>
    summarise(AWHP = sum(awhp_hhw), TES_SOC = sum(.data[[TES_var]])) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(AWHP, TES_SOC),
      names_to = "meter",
      values_to = "value") |>
    ggplot(aes(hour, value, color = meter)) +
        geom_line() +
        facet_grid(building ~ month, scales = "free") +
        labs(title = glue("Aggregated hourly HHW load served - {scen_desc}"), y = "Heating load (W)")
    return(plt)
}
```

```{r aggregated timeseries, szn, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
TES_var = "TES_charge"
plt_szn = function(df, scen, equip_scenarios) {
  scen_desc = equip_scenarios$desc[scen]
  plt = df |>
    filter(eq_scen_id == scen) |>
    mutate(quarter = quarter(datetime), hour = hour(datetime)) |>
    mutate(season = case_when(
      quarter == 1 ~ "Jan-Mar",
      quarter == 2 ~ "Apr-Jun",
      quarter == 3 ~ "Jul-Sep",
      quarter == 4 ~ "Oct-Dec",
    )) |>
    mutate(season = fct_reorder(season, quarter)) |>
    select(building, season, hour, awhp_hhw, .data[[TES_var]]) |>
    group_by(building, season, hour) |>
    summarise(AWHP = sum(awhp_hhw), TES_SOC = sum(.data[[TES_var]])) |>
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(AWHP, TES_SOC),
      names_to = "Meter",
      values_to = "value") |>
    ggplot(aes(hour, value, color = Meter)) +
        geom_line() +
        facet_grid(building ~ season, scales = "free") +
        labs(title = glue("Aggregated hourly HHW load served - {scen} -  {scen_desc}"), y = "Heating load (W)")
    return(plt)
}
```

```{r sample_days_hr, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
dat = results_all |>
  mutate(date = date(datetime)) |>

emissions_var = "elec_emissions" #elec_emissions

# plot_tes_control_scenarios = tes_control_scenarios |> add_column(tes_sizing = "Full")

plot_dates_emissions = dat |>
  filter(date %in% plot_dates$date) |>
  # select(building, eq_scen_id, desc, date, datetime, quarter, elec_emissions) |>
  summarize(elec_emissions = sum(.data[[emissions_var]]), .by = c(building, eq_scen_id, desc, date, quarter))

plot_dates_baseline_emissions = plot_dates_emissions |>
  filter(desc == "No TES") |>
  rename(elec_emissions_base = elec_emissions) |>
  select(building, date, elec_emissions_base)

plot_dates_emissions = plot_dates_emissions |>
  filter(desc != "No TES") |>
  left_join(plot_dates_baseline_emissions, by = c("building", "date")) |>
  mutate(elec_emissions_diff = 100*(elec_emissions - elec_emissions_base)/elec_emissions_base,
  building = as.double(building)) |>
  filter(abs(elec_emissions_diff) > 1e-1) |>
  inner_join(plot_dates, by = c("building", "date")) |>
  mutate(x = force_tz(ymd_h(str_c(as.character(date), " 11 PM")), "US/Pacific"), y = Inf) |>
  mutate(season_date = str_c(season, " (", date, ")")) |>
  mutate(quarter = ifelse(season == "Peak Day", 0, quarter)) |>
  left_join(select(equip_scenarios, eq_scen_id, tes_sizing, tes_control_id), by = "eq_scen_id")

plt_days = function(df, id, dates) {

  peakdate = dates |>
    filter(building == id, season == "Peak Day") |>
    select(date) |> pull()
  
  df = df |>
    filter(building == id) |>
    mutate(season = ifelse(date == peakdate, "Peak Day", season),
        quarter = ifelse(date == peakdate, 0, quarter)) |>
    filter(date %in% filter(dates, building == id)$date) |>
    mutate(season_date = str_c(season, " (", date, ")")) |>
    mutate(awhp_charging = ifelse(TES_charge_delta > 0, TES_charge_delta, 0)) |>
    mutate(awhp_load = awhp_hhw - awhp_charging) #|>
    # left_join(select(summary, building, desc, AWHP_size), by = c("building", "desc"))
    # left_join(plot_dates_emissions, by = c("building", "desc", "date")) |>
  #   select(eq_scen_id, desc, quarter, season_date, datetime, date, awhp_load, TES_charge, awhp_hhw, AWHP_size)
  # print(df)

  # hp_on_ctrl = df |>
  #   group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id) |>
  #   mutate(on = operate_hp_tes, group = cumsum(on != lag(on, default = FALSE))) |>
  #   filter(on == TRUE) |>
  #   group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id, season_date, quarter, group) |>
  #   summarize(xmin = min(datetime), xmax = max(datetime)+hours(1))

  base_loads_plot = df |>
    pivot_longer(cols = c(hhw, chw), names_to = "base_load", values_to = "base_load_value") |>
    ggplot() +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, base_load_value, color=base_load)) +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, hr_max_cap_h, color="hr_max_cap_h"), linetype=2) +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, hr_min_cap_h, color="hr_min_cap_h"), linetype=3) +
      labs(x = "", y = "(W)", color="", title = glue("Building {id}")) +
      scale_x_datetime(labels = NULL) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("hhw" = "red", "chw" = "blue", "hr_max_cap_h" = "red", "hr_min_cap_h" = "red"), labels = c("hhw" = "HHW", "chw" = "CHW", "hr_max_cap_h" = "Max WWHP capacity", "hr_min_cap_h" = "Min WWHP capacity")) +
      facet_grid(. ~ reorder(season_date, quarter), scales = "free_x") +
      theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

  # emissions_plot = df |>
  #   ggplot() +
  #     geom_line(aes(datetime, elec_emissions_rate, color="Emissions"), linetype = 2) +
  #     labs(x = "", y = "(gC02e/Wh)", color="") +
  #     scale_x_datetime(labels = NULL) +
  #     scale_color_manual(values = c("Emissions" = "gray")) +
  #     facet_grid(. ~ reorder(season_date, quarter), scales = "free_x") +
  #     theme(strip.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

  loads_plot = df |>
    pivot_longer(
        cols = c(hr_hhw, TES_charge, awhp_hhw, awhp_chw), # TES_load),
        names_to = "equipment",
        values_to = "load") |>
    mutate(equipment = case_when(
      equipment == "awhp_hhw" ~ "AWHP HHW",
      equipment == "awhp_chw" ~ "AWHP CHW",
      equipment == "hr_hhw" ~ "HR HHW",
      equipment == "TES_charge" ~ "TES SOC"
      )) |>
    ggplot() +
      # geom_rect(data = hp_on_ctrl, aes(xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax, ymin=0, ymax=Inf, fill="HP Enabled (Calc. Hrs)"), alpha=0.1) +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, load, color = equipment)) +
      geom_text(data = filter(plot_dates_emissions, building ==id),
        aes(x, y, label = str_c(percent(elec_emissions_diff/100, accuracy=0.1, style_positive = "plus"), " emissions")), vjust = 2, hjust = 1, size=3) +
      labs(x = "Hour", y = "Energy use (W)", color = "", fill = "", shape = "") +
      # geom_point(data = plot_tes_control_scenarios, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, shape = tes_legend), alpha=0, inherit.aes=FALSE) +
      scale_color_manual(
        values = c("HR HHW" = "red", "TES SOC" = "orange", "AWHP HHW" = "pink", "AWHP CHW" = "#56b4f6d0", "hr_max_cap_h" = "red", "hr_min_cap_h" = "red"),
        labels = c("hr_max_cap_h" = "Max WWHP capacity", "hr_min_cap_h" = "Min WWHP capacity")) +
      # scale_fill_manual(values = c("HP Enabled (Calc. Hrs)" = "green", "HP Enabled (OAT Reset)" = "blue", "Unintended HP Operation" = "orange", "HP Operation Over Max" = "red")) +
      scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%H") +
      # facet_nested(tes_sizing + tes_control_id ~ reorder(season_date, quarter), 
      facet_grid(reorder(desc, eq_scen_id) ~ reorder(season_date, quarter), 
      labeller = labeller(
        tes_sizing     = function(x) ifelse(x == "", "No TES", x),
        tes_control_id = function(x) ifelse(x == 0, "-", x)
      ),
      scales = "free_x") +
      theme(strip.text.x = element_blank())
    

  final_plot = base_loads_plot + plot_spacer() + 
    # emissions_plot + plot_spacer() + 
    loads_plot +
    plot_layout(ncol=1, heights = c(1, -0.1, 4))
  final_plot
}
```

```{r sample_days_awhp, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
plot_tes_control_scenarios = tes_control_scenarios  # |> add_column(tes_sizing = "Partial")

plot_dates_emissions = dat |>

  summarize(elec_emissions = sum(.data[[emissions_var]]), .by = c(building, eq_scen_id, desc, date, quarter))

plot_dates_baseline_emissions = plot_dates_emissions |>

plot_dates_emissions = plot_dates_emissions |>

  left_join(plot_dates_baseline_emissions, by = c("building", "date")) |>

  mutate(season_date = str_c(season, " (", date, ")")) |>
  mutate(quarter = ifelse(season == "Peak Day", 0, quarter)) |>
  left_join(select(equip_scenarios, eq_scen_id, tes_sizing, tes_control_id), by = "eq_scen_id")

plt_days = function(df, id, dates) {

  peakdate = dates |>
    filter(building == id, season == "Peak Day") |>
    select(date) |> pull()
  
  df = df |>
    filter(building == id,
    tes_sizing %in% c("2x Partial", "3x Partial")
    ) |>
    mutate(season = ifelse(date == peakdate, "Peak Day", season),
        quarter = ifelse(date == peakdate, 0, quarter)) |>
    filter(date %in% filter(dates, building == id)$date) |>
    mutate(season_date = str_c(season, " (", date, ")")) |>
    mutate(awhp_charging = ifelse(TES_charge_delta > 0, TES_charge_delta, 0)) |>
    mutate(awhp_load = awhp_hhw - awhp_charging) #|>
    # left_join(select(summary, building, desc, AWHP_size), by = c("building", "desc"))
    # left_join(plot_dates_emissions, by = c("building", "desc", "date")) |>
  #   select(eq_scen_id, desc, quarter, season_date, datetime, date, awhp_load, TES_charge, awhp_hhw, AWHP_size)
  # print(df)

  hp_on_ctrl = df |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id) |>
    mutate(on = operate_hp_tes, group = cumsum(on != lag(on, default = FALSE))) |>
    filter(on == TRUE) |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id, season_date, quarter, group) |>
    summarize(xmin = min(datetime), xmax = max(datetime)+hours(1))

  hp_on_oat = df |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id) |>
    mutate(on = (!(operate_hp_tes) & hp_tes != 0), group = cumsum(on != lag(on, default = FALSE))) |>
    filter(on == TRUE) |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id, season_date, quarter, group) |>
    summarize(xmin = min(datetime), xmax = max(datetime)+hours(1))

  hp_on_unintentional = df |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id) |>
    mutate(on = (hp_tes == 0 & awhp_hhw > 0), group = cumsum(on != lag(on, default = FALSE))) |>
    filter(on == TRUE) |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id, season_date, quarter, group) |>
    summarize(xmin = min(datetime), xmax = max(datetime)+hours(1))

  hp_on_over_max = df |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id) |>
    mutate(on = awhp_hhw - awhp_cap_h_total > 1e-3, group = cumsum(on != lag(on, default = FALSE))) |>
    filter(on == TRUE) |>
    group_by(desc, tes_sizing, tes_control_id, season_date, quarter, group) |>
    summarize(xmin = min(datetime), xmax = max(datetime)+hours(1))

  oat_plot = df |>
    ggplot() +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, oa_t, color="OAT"), linetype = 2) +
      labs(x = "", y = "(°C)", color="", title = glue("Building {id}")) +
      scale_x_datetime(labels = NULL) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("OAT" = "black")) +
      facet_grid(. ~ reorder(season_date, quarter), scales = "free_x") +
      theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

  emissions_plot = df |>
    ggplot() +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, elec_emissions_rate, color="Emissions"), linetype = 2) +
      labs(x = "", y = "(gC02e/Wh)", color="") +
      scale_x_datetime(labels = NULL) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("Emissions" = "gray")) +
      facet_grid(. ~ reorder(season_date, quarter), scales = "free_x") +
      theme(strip.text.x = element_blank(), axis.ticks.x = element_blank())

  loads_plot = df |>
    pivot_longer(
        cols = c(awhp_load, TES_charge, awhp_hhw), # TES_load),
        names_to = "equipment",
        values_to = "load") |>
    mutate(equipment = case_when(
      equipment == "awhp_hhw" ~ "AWHP (total)",
      equipment == "awhp_load" ~ "AWHP (load)",
      # equipment == "awhp_charging" ~ "AWHP (charging)",
      # equipment == "TES_load" ~ "TES discharge",
      equipment == "TES_charge" ~ "TES SOC"
      )) |>
    ggplot() +
      geom_rect(data = hp_on_ctrl, aes(xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax, ymin=0, ymax=Inf, fill="HP Enabled (Calc. Hrs)"), alpha=0.1) +
      geom_rect(data = hp_on_oat, aes(xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax, ymin=0, ymax=Inf, fill="HP Enabled (OAT Reset)"), alpha=0.1) +
      geom_rect(data = hp_on_unintentional, aes(xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax, ymin=0, ymax=Inf, fill="Unintended HP Operation"), alpha=0.1) +
      geom_rect(data = hp_on_over_max, aes(xmin=xmin, xmax=xmax, ymin=0, ymax=Inf, fill="HP Operation Over Max"), alpha=0.1) +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, load, color = equipment)) +
      geom_line(aes(datetime, awhp_cap_h_total, color="awhp_cap_h_total"), linetype=2) +
      geom_text(data = filter(plot_dates_emissions, building == id, tes_sizing %in% c("2x Partial", "3x Partial")),
        aes(x, y, label = str_c(percent(elec_emissions_diff/100, accuracy=0.1, style_positive = "plus"), " emissions")), vjust = 2, hjust = 1, size=3) +
      labs(x = "Hour", y = "Energy use (W)", color = "", fill = "", shape = "") +
      geom_point(data = plot_tes_control_scenarios, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, shape = tes_legend), alpha=0, inherit.aes=FALSE) +
      scale_color_manual(values = c("AWHP (load)" = "pink", "TES discharge" = "orange", "TES SOC" = "orange", "AWHP (charging)" = "pink", "AWHP (total)" = "red", "awhp_cap_h_total" = "red"), labels = c("awhp_cap_h_total" = "Max AWHP capacity")) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = c("HP Enabled (Calc. Hrs)" = "green", "HP Enabled (OAT Reset)" = "blue", "Unintended HP Operation" = "orange", "HP Operation Over Max" = "red")) +
      scale_x_datetime(date_labels = "%H") +
      facet_nested(tes_sizing + tes_control_id ~ reorder(season_date, quarter), 
      labeller = labeller(
        tes_sizing     = function(x) ifelse(x == "", "No TES", x),
        tes_control_id = function(x) ifelse(x == 0, "-", x)
      ),
      scales = "free_x") +
      theme(strip.text.x = element_blank())
    
  # tbl = select(equip_scenarios, eq_scen_id, desc) |>
  #   mutate(line = glue("{eq_scen_id}: {desc}")) |>
  #   pull(line) |>
  #   paste(collapse = "\n\n") |>
  #   str_replace_all(",", ",\n")

  final_plot = oat_plot + plot_spacer() + emissions_plot + plot_spacer() + loads_plot +
    plot_layout(ncol=1, heights = c(1, -0.3, 1, -0.3, 8)) #+
    # plot_annotation(caption = tbl, theme = theme(plot.caption.position = "plot", plot.caption = element_text(size = 8, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = -120, l = 945))))
  # collect_legends(final_plot)
  final_plot
}
```

# Abstract {.unnumbered}
The addition of thermal energy storage (TES) to shift thermal loads to off-peak periods of the day effectively reduces HVAC system energy costs, emissions, and peak electric demand. While cool thermal storage systems are well documented in the existing literature, this study analyzes TES for heating hot water systems. Heating hot water TES is increasingly common as designers switch from gas boilers to heat pumps and is more economical than chilled water TES due to higher system temperature differentials. Additionally, TES systems can be configured for a range of applications, including leveling design day peak loads, minimizing utility costs, reducing short-cycling related wear and tear, capturing capacity from non-simultaneous heat recovery, and improving heat pump efficiency. Current design guidance addressing these various applications is incomplete and dispersed across sources; this paper details appropriate rule-based control strategies that can be adopted for each application. We evaluate annual energy use and emissions for the proposed configurations using marginal grid emissions rates and a plant model with air-source heat pumps for primary heating. The model is analyzed over a dataset of measured heating hot water loads from six existing commercial buildings in California, covering a range of daily and seasonal load profile characteristics. Results show that the addition of TES can simultaneously reduce required heat pump capacity and operational carbon emissions, with up to 15% annual emissions reduction using the minimum tank size for load leveling. The magnitude of these savings is closely tied to both the sizing strategy and the variation in the control signal. For certain load profiles, further emissions reductions can be achieved by increasing the tank volume; while the cost of additional storage is not offset by a reduction in installed heat pump capacity, the carbon mitigation impact is comparable to that of electrifying from gas to electric heating in the first place. By identifying the impact of various sizing and control strategies on emissions across various building load profiles, this study provides actionable findings and recommendations in designing and implementing TES systems.

# Introduction

Thermal energy storage (TES) is an increasingly common strategy for shifting HVAC loads to favorable conditions for energy consumption or utility costs. It has historically been employed in chilled water (CHW) systems largely to reduce electricity costs and the installed size and cost of refrigeration equipment. As the industry decarbonizes heating systems by switching from gas boilers to heat pumps, there is a growing need to address these same concerns using heating hot water (HHW) TES. Prior research shows that most buildings’ hot water systems operate at low part loads the majority of the time [@rafteryInsightsHydronicHeating2024]. The addition of TES for peak load leveling can thus allow substantial downsizing of air-source heat pumps, resulting in considerable cost savings due to the high first cost of heat pumps. Additionally, since HHW systems typically operate with larger ΔTs than CHW loops, hot water TES provides more storage capacity for the same volume and first cost.

There is limited literature evaluating heat pump – particularly air-to-water heat pump (AWHP) – systems with hot water TES. One study demonstrated the cost effectiveness of a TES-integrated ground-source heat pump system using measured loads from a university campus with various charging control strategies [@ryanApplicationThermalEnergy2022]. Another pilot study installed AWHP with HHW TES systems in California single-family homes [@weigelTechnicalEvaluationAirtoWater2025]. There are additional papers demonstrating operational cost savings from chilled water TES, integrated either with heat pumps or traditional chillers, based on measured data [@woldekidanTechnoEconomicAnalysisAddition2025; @choOptimalControlStrategies2021; @khunStrategyEnergySavings2025; @rahmanFeasibilityThermalEnergy2011; @qiaoFieldTestingSimulation2026], but few use complete annual datasets. There is also a lack of research on the carbon impact of adding TES to a heat pump plant, particularly using marginal operating emissions rates which more accurately capture the variation in daily electricity generation emissions than average rates [@ryanMarginal2024]. @sultanCarbonMitigationPotential2023 simulated a residential CHW TES system and calculated 12% grid emissions reduction over one week of operation.

This paper applies and expands on existing ASHRAE guidance for sizing and controlling cooling TES systems [@glazerjasonASHRAEDesignGuide2019; @ashraeHandbook2024] to evaluate an all-electric heating plant consisting of air-to-water heat pumps and heating hot water TES. We model this using a dataset of full-year measured loads from 6 buildings to assess the contribution of load profile variation on equipment sizing. We quantify the carbon emissions impact of various sizing and control strategies and propose a framework for controlling AWHP-TES systems in order to maximize load shifting potential.

# Methods

## Inputs and Assumptions
This study uses one year of measurements of outside air temperature and conditioning loads gathered from the building automation systems of six buildings in San Francisco, California (ASHRAE Climate Zone 3C). Load data was either directly metered or calculated from flow meter and temperature sensor measurements. @fig-dataset_szn plots the average seasonal heating hot water (HHW) and chilled water (CHW) loads for each building in the dataset. Buildings A and B are academic buildings; C, D, and E are laboratory buildings; and F is a mixed-use laboratory/office building. 

HVAC energy consumption is modeled with a combination of AWHPs and thermal energy storage tanks. In the scenarios with no storage, the AWHPs are sized to serve the peak hourly heating load, and an air-cooled electric chiller is included to serve any excess chilled water loads. We used the performance data obtained from two different manufacturers to generate curves for heating capacity and coefficient of performance (COP) based on outside air temperature, shown in @fig-awhp_curves, for a nominal 211 kW (720 kBtu/h) modular unit at a HHW supply temperature of 54°C (130°F). 

Any analysis of load shifting – to optimize for an operational parameter such as cost or emissions beyond peak load leveling – is predicated on some form of cost signal to define appropriate charging or discharging periods. This is typically utility cost rates with the goal of minimizing operational cost, but could also be equipment operating efficiency in order to minimize energy consumption. This paper uses electricity use emissions as the cost signal, modeled using long-run marginal grid emissions rates for 2025 sourced from NLR’s Cambium 2024 dataset [@gagnonCambium2024Scenario2024]. This data is easily accessible and clearly demonstrates the tangible environmental impact of different system configurations. All analyzed buildings fall in the CAISO grid region, and we use the MidCase grid scenario. @fig-awhp_curves shows the distribution of hourly grid emissions factors in the selected dataset, highlighting the potential to substantially reduce emissions each day by shifting electrical loads to the hours around midday in this grid region.

## System Sizing

Sizing for AWHP-TES systems depends on the proportion of peak loads the tank is expected to satisfy, and there is a tradeoff between the TES capacity required to serve loads above the AWHP’s maximum capacity under peak load conditions versus the TES capacity available for load shifting. This interaction is described in detail in @casillasConsiderationsIntelligentlySizing2023. The ASHRAE Systems Handbook describes a standard method for chilled water storage which sizes the TES to minimize the total cooling equipment size, such that the latter can meet loads on the peak day by operating at maximum capacity continuously. This is called _partial storage_ (or load leveling) because the TES contributes only partially to the peak load and both chiller and tank must operate, in contrast to _full storage_ where the TES would be sized to fully meet loads (with the cooling plant disabled) during a predetermined on-peak (cost) period.

```{r fig-dataset_peakdays, eval = FALSE, include = FALSE}
    scale_y_continuous(labels=comma, sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * 3.412, name = "Load [kBtu/h]", labels=comma)) +
```

The NLR Decarbonizing Building Thermal Systems guide briefly discusses heating TES systems and recommends the same sizing strategies as a starting point for designers [@houssainyDecarbonizingBuildingThermal2024a]. It is also important to note that the peak day for TES sizing refers to the day with the largest aggregated total load, which does not always coincide with the day with the largest hourly load. (This is the case for building B, which is why the AWHP does not operate up to maximum capacity in the no-TES peak day plot in @fig-hp_priority).

This paper uses the partial storage sizing strategy for heating loads. While this method results in less load shifting flexibility during high load periods, it is the lowest first-cost scenario because it minimizes heat pump size with the smallest possible tank. Increasing TES capacity beyond this point rapidly escalates first costs as it does not allow any further first cost reduction in heat pump capacity. @fig-sizing represents an example peak day profile. The AWHP capacity is the sum of the peak day loads divided by 24 hours, and the TES capacity is the sum of the positive (or negative) difference between the hourly load and AWHP capacity. For simplicity, we assume constant AWHP capacity for sizing, determined at the lowest outside air temperature on the peak day (capacity varies based on hourly outside air temperature in the subsequent annual simulations). @tbl-equip_sizing lists the calculated equipment sizes. The tank volume is calculated using an 11°C (20°F) hot water ΔT and refers to the usable storage volume, which is dependent on the tank and diffuser geometry and stratification effectiveness and is typically less than the nominal tank volume. Common values for the figure of merit – a metric that incorporates these factors to define the usable volume – range from 80-90% of nominal volume [@glazerjasonASHRAEDesignGuide2019].

```{r fig-sizing}
#| fig-cap: "System sizing (Building B)"
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
id = "181"
peak_date = plot_dates |> filter(building == id, season == "Peak Day") |> pull(date)
ann = ymd_h("2022-12-19 20") # ymd_h("2023-02-27 24") for 180

design_oat = results_all |> filter(building == id, eq_scen_id == 3)|> distinct(design_oat) |> pull(design_oat)
hp_num = results_all |> filter(building == id, eq_scen_id == 3)|> distinct(hp_num_tes) |> pull(hp_num_tes)

hp_size = hp_num * interp1_zero(awhp_h_curve$oa_t, awhp_h_curve$cap_h, design_oat)

plot_results |>
  filter(building == id, desc == "No TES", date(datetime) == peak_date) |>
  mutate(AWHP = hp_size) |>
  select(datetime, hhw, AWHP) |>
  ggplot() +
    geom_line(aes(datetime, hhw/1000, color = "hhw")) +
    geom_line(aes(datetime, AWHP/1000, color = "AWHP")) +
    ggh4x::stat_difference(aes(x = datetime, ymin = hhw/1000, ymax = AWHP/1000), alpha=0.1, levels = c("Charging", "Discharging")) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("AWHP" = "red", "hhw" = "pink"), labels = c("hhw" = "Heating load")) +
    labs(y="Load [kW]", x="Hour", fill = "TES", color = "", subtitle = "x") +
    guides(color = guide_legend(direction = "horizontal"), fill = guide_legend(direction = "horizontal")) +
    theme(legend.position="top" , #c(1, 1.18)
        legend.justification="right",
        legend.background = element_blank(),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#ffffff"),
        axis.title.y.right = element_text(angle = 90)) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("Charging" = "green", "Discharging" = "orange")) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 500, 100), labels=comma,
    sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * 3.412, name = "Load [kBtu/h]", labels=comma)) +
```
